candidate.answerReason: The single discount leaves $6000 payable, while the successive discounts leave $6144. Their difference is $144.

methods.label: Compare the discounted bills
methods.explanation:
A successive discount applies to the amount remaining after the previous discount. A single \(40\%\) discount leaves \(60\%\) of the original bill, so the amount payable is
\[
10000(0.60)=6000
\]
dollars.

For the successive discounts, the \(36\%\) discount first leaves \(10000(0.64)=6400\) dollars. The \(4\%\) discount then leaves \(96\%\) of this reduced amount, giving \(6400(0.96)=6144\) dollars.

Because both plans start with the same bill, the difference between the discount amounts equals the difference between the final bills:
\[
6144-6000=144.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{144}\) dollars, choice B.
